PG.rationale: PG is a high-quality consumer staples franchise (#1/#2 market share in most categories, 70-year dividend streak, ~$84B in net sales) but the near-term fundamental picture is mixed. YoY growth remains positive (revenue +7.4%, EPS +5.8%) and the balance sheet is sound (equity $54.7B, liabilities/equity 1.35x). However, margin compression is the central concern: gross margin has fallen ~190bp from peak (51.4% in Q1 FY2025 to 49.5% in Q3 FY2026) and operating margin has eroded ~460bp (26.2% to 21.6%), driven by $1B commodity/logistics headwinds and $400M tariff costs. Sequential cash generation is declining (OCF QoQ -18.6%). Valuation has compressed meaningfully (PE 22.9x vs 26.5x a year ago, near 365-day low of 21.7x), but this repricing is justified by margin deterioration — the stock is fairly repriced for worse economics rather than undervalued. The earnings yield (4.4%) now matches the 10-year Treasury (4.45%), eliminating PG's quality premium over risk-free rates. The restructuring plan ($1.5B savings, 7,000 job cuts by FY2027) is a credible medium-term offset but not a dated near-term catalyst. Oil at $92.65 (+30%) remains a headwind. Net: franchise quality is high but fundamentals are deteriorating at the margin, valuation is fair not cheap, and no near-term catalyst exists to re-rate the stock. Score sits near neutral.
